title: The Left-Digit Effect: Why $9.99 Feels Cheaper

narration.timingStatus: word timestamps supplied with ElevenLabs narration; final word ends at 61.25275 seconds
narration.transcript: One store sold more sweaters at $39 than at 34. $5 more expensive and more people bought it. And no, those customers weren't confused. Their brains were doing exactly what brains do. Researchers put the same clothing on sale at three prices, 34, 39, 44. The $39 version beat them both. Here's why. You don't read $9.99 as $10. Your eyes hit the 9 first and stop. The 9 is the price. The 99 is decoration. That's the left digit effect. One digit does all the work and the other one just stands there making the first one look smaller. Now multiply that by every price in every store you walked into this week. The tag isn't telling you what it costs, it's telling you which number to look at. So is $9.99 a discount or a disguise? Tell me in the comments. And follow Oddly Logical for more strange things hiding in plain sight.
